title: DTOs, Zod & Input Validation
outcome: Validate untrusted input with Zod and DTO/boundary patterns while keeping transport validation distinct from business rules.
artifact: Reusable create/update/query schemas integrated into NestJS request handling with useful validation errors.
labSteps: List the exact fields accepted by create-task and reject unknown/invalid shapes deliberately.
Create a Zod schema and derive the TypeScript type instead of maintaining two divergent contracts.
Integrate validation at the NestJS boundary before the service receives data.
Create a partial update schema carefully and reason about omitted vs nullable fields.
Validate query parameters such as page size/sort values instead of trusting strings.
Send malformed requests and verify the error contract is actionable but does not expose internals.
failureModes: Duplicating client and server validation rules without a sharing strategy
Putting database existence checks into pure syntax schemas
Accepting arbitrary unknown keys into persistence calls
mastery: Can distinguish type checking from runtime validation
Can map Zod failures to HTTP responses
Can identify domain rules that belong after validation
principles: Validate external input at the application boundary before business logic trusts it.
Use schemas to produce both runtime checks and reusable TypeScript types where appropriate.
Distinguish transport validation from domain/business rules because they fail for different reasons.
Return validation errors that help clients correct input without exposing internal implementation details.
